question: What is the project code name used internally?
why: Used everywhere in place of customer or product names

question: In one paragraph, what is the deliverable (what gets built and handed over)?
What problem does it solve for the end user?
What stage is the project in (concept, design, prototype, qualification, production, sustaining)?
What are the next three milestones and their target dates?
What is the overall delivery or completion date?
How many units (or machines) are to be built, and over what period?
Is this a new design, a modification of an existing product, or a build to a customer design?
What existing products or earlier versions does it replace or resemble?
What are the three biggest technical risks the team sees today?
What are the three biggest schedule risks?
What has already been decided that should not be revisited?
What is still undecided that blocks progress?
What document defines the requirements (specification, statement of work, purchase order), with number and revision?
Which standards are called out, with their exact editions?
What deliverables besides hardware are required (reports, data items, manuals, drawings, certificates)?
Which design reviews or customer reviews are required, and when?
Which tests must the customer witness?
What acceptance criteria does the customer use to accept the product?
Who is the customer contact for technical questions, and for quality questions (role, not name)?
Are there penalties or incentives tied to dates or performance?
What has the customer said informally that is not yet in the written requirements?
Who is on the team, by role (project lead, mechanical, electrical, controls, quality, purchasing, test)?
Who has authority to approve design changes?
What is the budget, and how much is spent or committed so far?
Which parts or services are long-lead, and what are their quoted lead times?
Which suppliers are already chosen, and for what?
Which items are single-source?
Which outside labs or contractors are involved, and for what?
Which quality system does the company work under (AS9100, ISO 9001, ISO 13485, other)?
Where do controlled documents live (system name), and how are revisions released?
How are engineering changes requested and approved?
Is first article inspection required, and to what standard (for example AS9102)?
How are nonconformances recorded and dispositioned?
Are there customer flow-down clauses on suppliers (quality, counterfeit parts, export control)?
What records must be kept, and for how long?
Has the export-control officer classified the technical data (ITAR category, EAR ECCN, or not controlled)?
why: Decides what may leave the controlled environment

question: Which documents are marked export-controlled?
Is there CUI on the project, and which DFARS clauses apply (for example 252.204-7012)?
Are any team members or suppliers foreign persons for ITAR purposes, and is that managed?
Who is the prime contractor or end program office (role or code name only)?
Is AS9145 (aerospace APQP/PPAP) invoked?
Is configuration management to a specific standard required (EIA-649, MIL-HDBK-61)?
Are counterfeit-part controls flowed down (AS5553, DFARS 252.246-7007/7008)?
Is item unique identification (MIL-STD-130 UID) required, and where will the mark go?
Is a system safety analysis required (MIL-STD-882)?
Is a reliability prediction or FRACAS required?
Is environmental stress screening required in production, and to what profile?
Is DCMA or customer source inspection expected?
What packaging and marking requirements apply (MIL-STD-2073, MIL-STD-129)?
Are there human-factors requirements (MIL-STD-1472: weight, size, glove use)?
What is the device weight target and current estimate?
What are the outside dimensions target and current estimate?
Which source battery or batteries will feed the device (type, not maker if restricted)?
What is the input voltage range across full charge, empty, and cold?
What continuous and peak current can the source supply?
What device normally sits on the cable this unit replaces, and what does it draw?
Must the pass-through device keep full power while charging, and who gets priority?
What is the charging output: voltage, current limit, and what it connects to?
Is this unit a power source only, or does it control the radio battery charge?
What lithium-ion battery is being charged (chemistry, cell count, charge voltage, max charge current) per its data?
why: Charge limits come from the battery maker

question: What are the battery charge temperature limits, and who measures temperature?
What protection is on input and output (reverse polarity, short circuit, over-current, transients)?
What happens at hot-plug and in any connection order?
What is the quiescent current with nothing connected?
What efficiency and heat dissipation are expected at full load?
What output ripple and noise limits apply, and where are they measured?
Is there SMBus or other battery data, and what does the device do with it?
Is there USB on any port (2.0, Type-C, Power Delivery), and is it data, power or both?
Which connectors are used on each cable (family and keying, not proprietary pinouts)?
Are interface control documents available for the source battery, the radio battery and the radio adapter? Where?
Have comparable products (scavengers, radio power adapters) been benchmarked? Which?
Which part derating rules apply?
Has a thermal analysis been done for a hot day in the sun?
Has a design FMEA been done? Where is it?
Which MIL-STD-461 edition applies?
Which requirements are invoked (CE102, CS101, CS114, CS115, CS116, CS118, RE102, RS103, others)?
Are any limits tailored from the standard?
Is MIL-STD-464 or a system-level E3 requirement invoked?
Has pre-compliance scanning been done? Results summary?
What is the DC-DC converter switching frequency range (if not controlled)?
Are cables shielded, and how are shields terminated?
Is there filtering at each cable entry?
Which EMI lab, and when is the formal test?
Are an EMI test procedure and report required as data items?
Which MIL-STD-810 edition applies?
Has a life cycle environmental profile been written? Where?
Which methods and procedures are invoked, with levels?
What immersion depth and duration, and is there a temperature differential?
What operating and storage temperature ranges are required?
What vibration profile and duration?
What shock and drop requirements (heights, number of drops, surfaces)?
Sand and dust, salt fog, solar, humidity, altitude, fungus: which apply?
What is the test sequence and how many units?
What functional check is run before, during and after each test?
Which environmental lab, accreditation, and dates?
Enclosure material and process (machined, cast, extruded)?
Does one gasket do sealing and EMI, or two separate gaskets?
Gasket type, material and filler?
Is there a compression stop, and what compression range is targeted?
Has the gasket compression stack-up been run? Worst case and RSS results?
How many fasteners on the lid, and what spacing?
What finish on the housing, and which areas are masked?
What conductive finish on gasket lands and bonding points?
Paint or CARC required? Color?
How are connectors sealed and bonded to the enclosure?
What bonding resistance is required, and where is it measured?
Is there a vent membrane? Rated to what depth?
What leak test is used in production?
Which IPC class (IPC-A-610, J-STD-001, IPC-6012)?
Which conformal coating type, and which areas are masked?
Is potting or staking used?
Who builds the boards and cables, and are they AS9100 and IPC-trained?
Cable specification (shielded cable type, overmold or backshell)?
Are any key parts at risk of obsolescence?
